extracted.intended_audience: ICLR 2024 reviewers (conference peer reviewers in machine learning)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers evaluating submissions to ICLR 2024: how to read papers, structure reviews, apply ethical rules, engage in discussion, and make initial and final recommendations. Focused on assessing technical correctness, novelty, significance, and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely and substantive reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Your reviews are timely and substantive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet stated deadlines; provide reviews that are detailed and useful to area chairs and authors. Timely, high-quality reviews are recognized (top reviewers acknowledged, possible free registration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to Code of Ethics and Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviewers must read and adhere to the ICLR Code of Ethics and Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raise potential CoE violations when relevant; include discussion of ethical issues in submissions (not counted against page limit). Complete the CoE report when submitting your review (two-question form: potential violation? if yes, explain). For other violations (plagiarism, double submission, formatting), contact AC/SAC/PC or send a confidential comment with appropriate readership restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the paper thoroughly
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully read the entire paper and consult related work and citations to comprehensively evaluate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give yourself sufficient time to read; consult supplementary material as needed before asking authors questions since suplementary material can often answer questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify the objective of the work
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the goal of the paper (e.g., address a known application/problem, draw attention to a new application/problem, introduce/explain a new theoretical finding, or a combination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different objectives require different considerations about value and impact; be explicit about what the authors intended when judging significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess strong points
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify whether the submission is clear, technically correct, experimentally rigorous, reproducible, and presents novel findings (theoretical/algorithmic/etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List and explain specific strengths; give positive, constructive summary of main contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess weak points
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerate substantive weaknesses in clarity, correctness, experimental design, reproducibility, novelty, or other aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be as comprehensive as possible; distinguish minor issues from major flaws that affect the recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be mindful of biases and be open-minded
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid personal or topical biases; consider that a paper may be valuable to the broader ICLR community even if not interesting to you personally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an open spirit during reading and discussion; be willing to revise your recommendation based on discussion and author responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific question/problem clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine what specific question and/or problem the paper tackles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear, well-stated problem is a prerequisite for assessing relevance and contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach is well motivated and situated in literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the approach is well motivated and appropriately placed in the literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check citation/related-work placement; verify claims of novelty against prior work and ask for clarification when comparisons to prior results are unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims are supported: correctness and scientific rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether the paper supports its claims — theoretical or empirical — and whether results are correct and scientifically rigorous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check proofs for clarity and stated assumptions; verify empirical methodology, statistical significance, and that experiments support claimed conclusions. Ask for evidence or corrections if reasoning or derivations are unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance and contribution to the community
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the significance: does the paper contribute new knowledge and sufficient value to the ICLR community?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significance does not require state-of-the-art numbers; value can be empirical, theoretical, or practical. Explicitly justify why the work is or is not sufficiently valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review structure and required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the review to include a summary of the paper's claimed contributions, a list of strong and weak points, a clear initial recommendation (accept/reject) with 1–2 key reasons, supporting arguments, questions for the authors, and constructive feedback to improve the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be positive and constructive in the summary; make clear which points affect your decision versus which are suggestions for improvement. Use the review to help authors even if the paper is rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting additional experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may ask for additional experiments but these should not significantly change the content of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should be limited in scope and aimed at validating existing results rather than demanding new directions. Avoid asking for large-scale experiments that reframe the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use supplementary material judiciously
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary material is optional to read but may answer questions arising from the main paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider looking at supplementary content before asking authors for clarification that is already provided there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and reporting policy/ethics violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If you detect a possible policy or CoE violation, flag it in the CoE report submitted with your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For other policy violations (plagiarism, double submission, formatting), contact the AC/SAC or PC or use confidential comments; the AC will work with the PC and ethics board to resolve CoE cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage actively in discussion and be open to changing recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in the asynchronous discussion phase with reviewers, authors, and ACs; be open to changing your initial recommendation based on discussion and author revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize yourself with other reviewers' feedback; discussions are crucial and may lead to updating scores or recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Borderline-paper meetings participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Area Chairs may schedule virtual meetings for borderline papers; reviewers should attend when requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend scheduled meetings when your paper is called for borderline discussion; ACs will facilitate and may leverage attendance information when making decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a clear final recommendation with rationale and changes noted
rubrics_metrics.description: After discussion (and possible author revisions), update your review with a final recommendation and state the reasoning and what did/didn’t change your recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state how discussion or author updates affected your view; this helps ACs in decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate experimental methodology and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that experiments include sufficient methodological details (e.g., data, hyperparameters, number of runs), fair baseline comparisons, proper tuning, and statistical significance where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask for missing experimental details needed for reproducibility (e.g., initialization, reward structure, architecture, tuning procedure). Flag unfair comparisons (e.g., uneven tuning or inappropriate baselines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate theoretical soundness and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify theoretical claims, proofs, and assumptions for correctness and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request clearer statements of assumptions, steps in proofs, and definitions; point out unclear derivations or missing conditions that affect validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess novelty vs prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether claimed theorems, algorithms, or results are novel relative to cited prior work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When novelty is unclear, ask authors to clarify differences and explicitly cite relevant previous results; question reused or previously-known results presented as new.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing clarity, precision, and minor corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate and point out imprecise language, unclear notation, typos, and organization issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide minor corrections and suggestions (e.g., wording changes, section reordering, notation fixes) that improve readability; note which are cosmetic vs which affect substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not treat lack of SOTA as automatic rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission not achieving state-of-the-art results is not by itself grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge papers on whether they convincingly demonstrate new, relevant, and impactful knowledge; explain why non-SOTA work still brings value or why it does not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparisons to very recent or non-peer-reviewed work
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are not required to compare to contemporaneous papers published within four months prior to the deadline or to papers exclusively on arXiv; reviewers should use judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define 'contemporaneous' as published in proceedings within four months of deadline; if in doubt about omissions of recent work, discuss with your Area Chair.
